name: adv_audio_bad
title: torchaudio keyword-spotting classifier - eight planted defects
origin: the defective twin of adv_audio_clean, hardening round 1, 2026-09-13
note: The flat-script shape research audio code is usually written in. MLView finds ten of the eleven findings these eight defects imply; the one it misses is MLV205, because the accumulator is reset inside the epoch loop rather than above it (finding DGRG-04).

expected.why: every epoch sees the speakers in file-listing order, so the batches stay correlated and the gradient estimate is biased

expected.defect: num_workers=4 on a module-level loader in a file with no __main__ guard
expected.why: on spawn platforms every worker re-imports the module and re-runs the whole script, including the training loop

expected.defect: the same, for the validation loader
expected.why: one finding per loader is correct here - each construction is its own footgun

expected.defect: the same, for the test loader
expected.why: one finding per loader is correct here
the three partitions are a different three partitions on every run, so no two runs are comparable

expected.defect: nothing seeds torch, numpy or random
expected.why: the split, the initialisation and the dropout masks all move between runs

expected.defect: CosineAnnealingLR is stepped once per batch instead of once per epoch
expected.why: the whole cosine cycle completes inside the first epoch, so the remaining nineteen epochs train at the learning-rate floor and nothing raises

expected.defect: the epoch loss is accumulated as a live tensor
expected.why: running is created at line 101, inside the epoch loop but outside the batch loop, so every batch of the epoch keeps its autograd graph alive - the canonical per-epoch accumulator, and the shape MLV205's `_defined_outside` guard currently skips

expected.defect: the model is moved to DEVICE at line 88 but no batch anywhere in the file is; MLView reports the validation loop (line 64) and not the training loop (line 102), which carries the identical defect
expected.why: a CPU tensor fed to a CUDA module raises at run time on the first batch
AudioCNN carries two BatchNorm2d layers and a Dropout, so validation both drops activations and keeps updating the running statistics with validation data

expected.defect: validate() is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: gradients are tracked through the whole validation and test sets for nothing

forbidden.why: neither evaluation loader shuffles - both pass shuffle=False explicitly
the validation loader is not a training loader
the test loader is not a training loader
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is called at line 104, before the forward pass
the order is zero_grad (104) -> backward (108) -> step (109)
there is no no_grad block anywhere in this file, so backward cannot be inside one
there is no GradScaler and no autocast in this project
there is no gradient clipping in this project at all
AudioCNN.forward returns the raw classifier output; no softmax precedes CrossEntropyLoss
DEVICE is chosen by torch.cuda.is_available() at line 18
both nn.Module subclasses call super().__init__() on their first line
every submodule is a plain attribute or lives inside nn.Sequential
torch.save is given model.state_dict() at line 115 and there is no torch.load in this file

unsupported.defect: not a defect - recorded because model.train() is inside the epoch loop and validate() never switches modes, so the pair MLV301/MLV303 describes this file's mode handling and only one half of it exists
unsupported.why: MLV303 (train mode never restored) is a later-tier rule.
